body:
### Why

The work brief (`board.brief`) says to run `test --all` **and** "the test commands its `solace.toml` declares". `solace.toml` can't say which `[commands]` are tests, so agents guess. In task:c00c45bce4291567's work run the agent ran `test --all`, then `rust-unit`, `rust-board-tests`, `rust-lockdown-tests`, `rust-acceptance`, `spacing_parity`, `cargo-fmt-check`, `cargo-test` and `layout_audit`. `rust-unit` and `cargo-test` are the same suite as `test --all`, and the two `rust-*-tests` commands are parts of it. Then it ran most of them again after a one-line fix.

### Change

- A `[commands]` entry can be marked `test = true`, like `allowed_in_reviews`. The key is optional and defaults to false.
- The work brief names the marked commands of each project the task covers: "Before `task done`, after your last change, run `test --all` in each project with symbol-held source, and `run <name>` for: rust-acceptance, spacing_parity." If a project has no marked commands, the brief leaves that part out. It drops "the test commands its `solace.toml` declares".
- Propose marking `rust-acceptance` and `spacing_parity` in solace-cli's `solace.toml` (a settings `write` with `reason`). They are the only declared suites that `test --all` doesn't run.
- Update `board::tests.briefs_hold_what_the_agent_needs_as_text`, and record a decision.

### Done when

A work brief for a solace-cli task names exactly `rust-acceptance` and `spacing_parity`, and says to run them once, after the last change.
title: briefs: name the test commands to run
